clues: In third-party tests running the LTX-2.3 Fast model, its hardware generated a 1080p, six-second video clip in roughly 9 to 12 seconds.
Its clients include trading firm Virtu Financial, data center firm Equinix, and Japanese sovereign AI infrastructure venture ai&.
Alongside system hardware, it licenses proprietary RISC-V CPU cores and AI accelerator IP to chipmakers like Samsung and LG.
It rejected takeover bids of up to $5B from Intel and Qualcomm after proving its systems could run open-weight models from DeepSeek.
Its system lineup spans add-in cards, developer workstations, and complete Galaxy racks built around an open-source software stack.
Led by legendary chip architect Jim Keller, this AI hardware firm raised $1.5 billion in Series E funding at a $6.2 billion valuation.
